translations.adaptations: C double coefficients, polynomial expression order and branch structure are retained. Rust bool replaces int invert. The four original expl(-z*z)/z multiply expressions call a private portable high/low-double helper: the argument is first evaluated as f64, exp/divide/multiply are rounded to a 64-bit significand with separate exponent scaling for subnormals. This emulates the GNU reference long double evaluation; one observed ErfC output differs by 1 ULP, so bit-exact extended precision is not claimed. Full original Boost license notice is preserved.

integration: BlastScoreBlk.gbp: Option<BlastGumbelBlk> and core modules have been added by parent. BlastGumbelBlk preserves all source scalar fields.

Call blast_gumbel_blk_calc for selected BLOSUM62 gap costs, then populate gbp.db_length from database length/override in source units: divide nucleotide subject total by three for tblastn, as blast_setup.c does.
BLOSUM62_VALUES is reused from blast_protein_matrix; no additional protein matrix tables are translated. Unsupported-matrix diagnostic enumeration retains original enabled names.

Private HighLow arithmetic is a Rust-only compatibility adapter for four extended expressions, not a newly translated source function. The source uses DOUBLE everywhere else. GNU 64-bit-significand long double is the measured reference; target-native long-double differences are not silently presented as parity.

Numerical residual: ErfC(6.78671432911633232) differs by 1 ULP from GNU original C. All 8640 checked Spouge outputs were bit-identical and 360 cutoff scores exact; end-to-end and cross-platform comparison remain required.
numerical_compatibility_note: The known one-double-ULP ErfC difference comes from reference glibc expl differing from correctly rounded extended arithmetic at that input; see upstream/numerical-compatibility/README.md. Universal bitwise libm parity is not claimed.
